summary.one_liner: Achievement-NFT minter. One design-breaking bug: the NFT local id is the achievement key, so any achievement can only be minted ONCE collection-wide — the second player to earn 'first_grid' panics. Delivery pattern (try_deposit_or_abort) is correct.
asset_inventory: minter badge (game server, hot — mints NFTs)
trust_boundaries: game server (holds minter badge, calls mint_nft / mint_nft_to)
owner (cold badge — can revoke/rotate minter, enable burn, update NFT data)

findings.title: NFT local id == achievement key → each achievement mintable only ONCE collection-wide
findings.what: mint_nft sets the NFT's NonFungibleLocalId to the caller-supplied nft_id, documented as 'the game achievement key (e.g. first_grid)'. Non-fungible local ids must be unique per resource. But the SAME achievement (e.g. 'first_grid') is earned by MANY players — so the id 'first_grid' can be minted exactly once across the entire collection. The 2nd player to unlock 'first_grid' triggers a duplicate-id mint, which PANICS (the resource manager rejects duplicate local ids). Additionally NonFungibleLocalId::string(nft_id).unwrap() panics on a malformed/oversized id (>64 bytes or invalid chars).
findings.why: This breaks the core use case: an achievement NFT collection where multiple players earn the same achievement. As written, only the first player ever gets each achievement NFT; everyone after fails. This will surface immediately in Phase 2 the moment two players earn the same achievement.
findings.suggested_direction: Make the local id unique per (player, achievement) — e.g. hash(account + game_key) or an auto-incrementing integer id, and keep game_key as a DATA field (it already is) for catalog linkage. Validate/parse the id with a non-panicking path (return an error or assert with a clear message) instead of .unwrap().

findings.title: MintNftEvent.recipient records the component's own address, not the player
findings.what: MintNftEvent.recipient = Runtime::global_component().address() — the component's own address, not the actual recipient. Same self-referential bug as MemeGameVault F-002. Note that mint_nft_to DOES know the real account (it's a parameter) but calls mint_nft internally, so the event still logs the component address even when the true recipient is known.
findings.why: Any indexer reading MintNftEvent.recipient to know who received an achievement NFT gets the component address every time — useless. mint_nft_to has the correct address available and should thread it into the event.
findings.suggested_direction: Thread the recipient through: have mint_nft_to pass the account into the event (or emit the event from mint_nft_to with the real account), and for the bare mint_nft path (caller deposits) either drop the recipient field or document that attribution is off-chain via the tx.

findings.title: Unbounded minting authority on a hot minter badge
findings.what: The minter badge (held by the game server, described as hot / revocable) can mint unlimited NFTs with arbitrary data (name, rarity, icon_url all caller-supplied). No per-call limit, no rate limit, no allowlist of valid game_keys/rarities on-chain.
findings.why: A compromised minter badge can spam-mint arbitrary 'achievements' with any rarity/name, diluting/forging the collection. Mitigated by owner being able to rotate the minter (minter updatable_by OWNER) + revoke, but detection depends on off-chain monitoring. Same badge-custody class as MemeGameVault F-001.
findings.suggested_direction: Keep the minter badge tightly custodied (the server wallet). Consider an on-chain allowlist of valid game_keys/rarities, or move minting behind a bounded per-epoch cap, if the collection's integrity matters. At minimum, monitor MintNftEvent volume + alert on anomalies (once N-002 is fixed so events are attributable).

findings.title: Collection icon_url locked — can never be repointed
findings.what: The collection metadata icon_url => https://memegrid.radixguild.com/nfts/collection.svg is `locked`, immutable for the resource's life. (Per-NFT icon_url is a data field, updatable only if the owner later enables non_fungible_data_updater.)
findings.why: If the icon host moves or the domain lapses, the collection icon breaks in every wallet forever. Same class as MemeGameVault F-004 + guild-escrow BUG-6. Name/symbol locked is correct; icon_url locked is a foot-gun.
findings.suggested_direction: Grant a metadata_setter role (owner badge) for icon_url, or host on IPFS with an immutable CID so locked is safe.

checklist_coverage.note: get_* PUBLIC; mint_nft / mint_nft_to restrict_to [minter, OWNER]. minter updatable_by OWNER (equal-or-higher). mint_roles + burn_roles + data_update_roles all gate updaters behind the owner badge. Least-privilege + correct.

mint_nft_to makes ONE external call (account.try_deposit_or_abort) AFTER the mint + total_minted increment are complete — state finalised before the external call. No pre-mutation state exposed to a callback.
No Decimal math. total_minted is a u64 counter (+= 1); overflow is unreachable in practice (would need 1.8e19 mints).

The string-id-collision bug (N-001) is the central issue — user-supplied id + unwrap + per-achievement (not per-player) uniqueness. NFT bucket is returned (mint_nft) or deposited (mint_nft_to); no lost-bucket path.
No phases. Finding is event-correctness (self-referential recipient), not state integrity.

One external call — account.try_deposit_or_abort — is the CORRECT on-chain delivery pattern (atomic; aborts cleanly if the account deny-lists deposits). Contrast with the guild-escrow BUG-7 caller-manifest delivery gap; this blueprint does delivery right.

Not upgradeable (Fixed owner). NFT data non_fungible_data_updater = deny_all (updater_updater = owner), so achievements are immutable unless the owner later enables updates — reasonable. Finding is locked collection icon_url.
Minter badge = unbounded mint authority (N-003). Owner can rotate/revoke it (minter updatable_by OWNER) — a revoke path exists, which is good. Custody of the hot minter badge is the risk.

pattern_conformance.note: mint_nft_to deposits directly to the player account atomically — the correct pattern the guild escrow lacks. Strong.
minter role updatable_by OWNER + mint_roles minter_updater = owner → owner can rotate/revoke the hot minter badge.
id = achievement key → collides across players (N-001).

test_coverage_gaps: N-001 regression: two players earning the SAME achievement (same game_key) — asserts unique ids (currently panics on the 2nd).
mint_nft with an oversized / invalid nft_id string — asserts a clean error instead of an unwrap panic.
mint_nft_to to an account that rejects deposits — asserts the atomic abort (NFT not minted, no partial state).
auth: mint attempted without minter/owner badge — refused.
N-002: assert what MintNftEvent.recipient actually contains.
open_questions: N-001 is the blocker: what is the intended NFT id scheme? If each (player, achievement) should be a distinct NFT, the id must incorporate the account (or be an auto-increment) — the achievement key alone cannot be the id. Confirm before deploy; the current scheme fails on the second earner of any achievement.

N-003: is on-chain rarity/game_key validation wanted, or is trusting the server-held minter badge acceptable for a game NFT? Likely acceptable at test scale; revisit if the NFTs acquire secondary-market value.
This was a human-executed checklist pass; a CLI run against the exact source yields the attestable source_hash.
